bug_semantics: CWE-502 incomplete pickle allowlist in nltk/picklesec.py: AllowlistUnpickler.find_class admits a global when the module string matches allowed_modules (prefix) or an exact (module, name) pair, then calls pickle.Unpickler.find_class. It never rejects a dotted name, so protocol>=4 getattr-chains names such as sklearn.os.system out of an allowed namespace. TransitionParser.parse loads caller-supplied models via allowlisted_pickle_load(allowed_modules=numpy/scipy/sklearn), so a crafted model executes arbitrary callables.
flaw_origin: The advisory sink is the module-only AllowlistUnpickler, not the earlier warn-and-execute pickle_load. GitHub squash merge f26b3753038d937b68145daf15e9636f8451053c (#3631, 2026-07-01) first put that class on nltk/nltk default history; parent 8493007b3ec04bfa132ed5ca9cbecf127ecc9eda has RestrictedUnpickler/WarningUnpickler only. The squash decomposes to public PR member 7c233bdb55d394fe7f8cdd87b62ad08040e0d922 (2026-06-18), which first wrote find_class as `if (module, name) in allowed_globals or _module_allowed(module): return super().find_class(module, name)`. Parent 16a32d680d070254d5744e33fa83f9c0056d5a1f still lacks AllowlistUnpickler. Later PR bullets (tests, punkt helper, Copilot string-guard) did not add the dotted-name check. v3.10.0–v3.10.2 keep that find_class at the advisory lines; c3e37113742a1ebeeb4f2ca58941f320f98805ea (2026-08-10) first rejects dotted names and tightens namespace resolution.

reasoning: The published CVE is a real incomplete-remediation pickle RCE: an allowlist that checks only the module string and then lets Unpickler.find_class getattr-chain dotted names. That find_class was first written in public PR member 7c233bdb55d394fe7f8cdd87b62ad08040e0d922 (human LiteshGhute, no AI markers on that commit object) and landed via squash f26b3753038d937b68145daf15e9636f8451053c.
